title: Callback patterns and error-first callback history (overview)
learningObjectives: Explain callback patterns and error-first callback history (overview) and reason about JavaScript execution and function behaviour.

understand.concept: A callback is a function passed to another function for later execution. Older Node.js APIs commonly used error-first callbacks where the first argument is an error and later arguments carry results. Promises and async/await are now common alternatives for composable asynchronous flows.
understand.whyItMatters: Recognising callback patterns helps when maintaining older code and integrating APIs. Error-first conventions make failure handling explicit but deeply nested callbacks can become difficult to read.
understand.analogy: A callback is an instruction left with another operation to run when that operation reaches a certain point.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scope, execution, identity, and scheduling follow language and engine semantics.

explain.narrative: The callback receives null for the error and the record as the result, following the error-first convention.

practise.guidedTask: Write a callback API that returns either an error or a result. Then wrap it in a Promise and compare the calling code.
practise.independentTask: Create a small example that demonstrates the concept, test edge cases, and explain the execution or reference behaviour in your own words.

questions.prompt: In an error-first callback, what is conventionally the first argument?
options: An error value or null when there is no error
questions.answer: An error value or null when there is no error
questions.explanation: The first callback argument reports an error; null conventionally indicates success.

questions.prompt: What is a sound way to learn a language runtime concept?
options: Trace the relevant bindings, calls, and references
Memorise one output without understanding why
Assume all functions and objects behave identically
questions.answer: Trace the relevant bindings, calls, and references
questions.explanation: Tracing execution and references helps explain behaviour and predict edge cases.
